cases.description: The source says 'Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him'. The faulty Urdu draft drops both negation markers (نہ), which reverses the meaning entirely. RajiAI must flag this as a high-severity negation change — and offer evidence only, never a verdict.
cases.draft_text: اسے اونگھ آتی ہے اور نیند آتی ہے۔
cases.source_text: Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him.
cases.title: Missing negation — Ayat al-Kursi (Quran 2:255)

cases.description: A numeric value is altered between source and draft, including an Arabic-Indic digit variant (٩٩ → ٩٨), which RajiAI normalizes before comparing.

cases.description: A distinctive proper name present in the source is absent from the draft. RajiAI flags the missing token with evidence; the reviewer decides whether the omission matters.

cases.description: Source and draft carry the same meaning with equivalent wording. RajiAI should raise zero flags here. A quiet result is a correct result.

cases.source_text: And He is the Most High, the Most Great. There is no compulsion in religion.

Partial negation dropped — 'nor' removed
cases.description: Only one half of a 'neither/nor' pair survives in the draft. Marker count goes 2 → 1, so RajiAI must flag high-severity negation. A tough partial-drop case.
cases.source_text: Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him.
cases.draft_text: Neither drowsiness or sleep overtakes Him.

cases.title: Negation added by the draft
cases.description: The draft inserts 'not', reversing the meaning in the opposite direction. RajiAI must flag medium-severity added negation. Note: a low-severity key-term flag on 'loves'/'love' may also appear (no stemming) — a good false-alarm demo for the reviewer.
cases.source_text: Indeed, Allah loves the doers of good.
cases.draft_text: Indeed, Allah does not love the doers of good.

cases.title: Double negative flattened
cases.description: 'not uncommon' becomes 'common'. Marker count goes 1 → 0, so RajiAI must flag high-severity negation. A low key-term flag on 'uncommon'/'common' may also appear (no stemming) — reviewer marks it false alarm.
cases.source_text: It is not uncommon for the seeker to stumble.
cases.draft_text: It is common for the seeker to stumble.

cases.title: Number changed across digit scripts
cases.description: 99 becomes ٩٨ (Arabic-Indic digits). RajiAI normalizes both scripts to ASCII before comparing, so it must flag a high-severity number change.

cases.title: Number word dropped — 'five' removed
cases.description: The number checker only reads digits, not number words — a documented limitation. The new key-term coverage still surfaces the dropped 'five' as a low-severity flag so the reviewer sees it.
cases.source_text: Pray the five daily prayers: Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha.
cases.draft_text: Pray the daily prayers: Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha.

cases.title: Name respelled — Hurairah vs Hurayrah
cases.description: Same narrator, different transliteration. RajiAI cannot know they match, so it must surface 'hurairah' as a medium key-term flag. The reviewer — not the tool — decides it is the same person. A perfect 'human decides' case.
cases.source_text: Narrated by Abu Hurairah: seek knowledge.
cases.draft_text: Narrated by Abu Hurayrah: seek knowledge.

cases.title: Narrator dropped in Arabic
cases.description: أبي هريرة (Abu Hurairah) is dropped from an Arabic narration while البخاري stays. The Arabic-script name heuristic must flag it as medium.
cases.source_text: رواه البخاري عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه

cases.title: Dropped 'Say' — Surah Al-Ikhlas (112:1), found by manual testing
cases.description: The draft drops the opening imperative 'Say' (قُل) and weakens 'Indivisible' to 'divisible'. The name check flags 'indivisible' (medium); the key-term coverage flags 'say' (low). Added after Taha caught this miss by hand-testing on 2026-10-04.
